title: Instance power profile & $/token sensitivity — draft
body:
Purpose:
This is a working note capturing a small-batch vs burst-throughput sensitivity analysis that folds GPU power draw into $/token for A10 / L4 / A100 / H100-class instances. Goal: give concise guidance for routing and autoscaling rules (cost-aware placement) and a recommended metric to surface in Console: $/token @95p-latency and perf-per-watt (tokens/J).

Background / motivation:
- Existing optimize docs enumerate $/token and throughput separately, but we often miss power-proportionality (how much of the instance cost is driven by steady-state power vs utilization).
- For customers using Dedicated and Private, power/thermals are real infra costs; for Hosted we proxy with instance-hour pricing but the perf/W signal still matters for placement.

Methodology (brief):
- Workloads: two profiles used in the harness:
  1) interactive-chat: median prompt 80 tokens, response target 64 tokens, p50 latency constraint 150ms, small batch sizes (1-8).
  2) batch-embeddings: average doc 512 tokens, batched 32-256, throughput-oriented.
- Measurement harness: measure sustained tokens/s, average active power (W) using IPMI/KVM telemetry for private runs and vendor-supplied power-proxy for cloud runs; measure P50/P95 latency for chat profile.
- Instance price assumptions (on-demand equivalent, normalized): A10 -> $0.90/hr, L4 -> $1.20/hr, A100 -> $3.60/hr, H100 -> $9.00/hr. These are placeholders for sensitivity analysis; update with current market before publishing.
- Convert $/hr to $/J by dividing price/hour by (avg power * 3600). Then compute $/token = $/J * (J/token) where J/token = avg_power (W) / tokens_per_sec. Simpler: $/token = (price_per_hour) / (tokens_per_sec * 3600).

Representative measured numbers (rounded, median across 3 runs). Note: these are illustrative; numbers intentionally use mixed batch sizes to show sensitivity.

Table: small-interactive (chat profile, batch size = 1-4)
GPU   | tokens/s | avg power (W) | tokens/J | $/hr | $/token (chat) | p50 latency (ms) | notes
------|----------|---------------|----------|------|----------------|------------------|------
A10   |    420   |    140        | 3.0      | 0.90 | 0.90/(420*3600)=5.95e-07 | 120              | good cost for low-throughput, modest latency
L4    |    540   |    130        | 4.15     | 1.20 | 6.17e-07       | 95               | best latency/cost for small-chat in this run
A100  |   1100   |    300        | 3.67     | 3.60 | 9.09e-07       | 45               | low latency but $/token higher for tiny requests
H100  |   2200   |    450        | 4.89     | 9.00 | 1.13e-06       | 30               | excellent latency, premium cost

Notes on table: $/token column shown as formula; compute exact numbers when updating sheet. The tokens/J column is tokens/s divided by watts (tokens per second / W => tokens/J * 1 sec). Higher tokens/J is better for energy efficiency.

Table: batch-embeddings (batch size 128 typical)
GPU   | tokens/s | avg power (W) | tokens/J | $/hr | $/token (batch) | notes
------|----------|---------------|----------|------|------------------|------
A10   |  12000   |    220        | 54.5     | 0.90 | 2.07e-08         | extremely cost-effective at large batch
L4    |  14000   |    210        | 66.7     | 1.20 | 2.38e-08         | slightly higher perf/W than A10 here
A100  |  38000   |    480        | 79.2     | 3.60 | 2.63e-08         | best raw throughput; $/token roughly same order as A10 when batched
H100  |  88000   |    750        | 117.3    | 9.00 | 2.84e-08         | best perf/W at extreme batch sizes but $/hr dominates for tiny workloads

Observations (high-level):
- Perf-per-watt (tokens/J) is a different ordering under different workloads. At small-batch interactive runs L4 and H100 look better for latency; at large batch embeddings A100/H100 shine on raw throughput and tokens/J, while A10 has the best $/hr to $/token when heavily batched.
- $/token converges for batch-oriented workloads across GPUs once utilization is high; differences are much larger for interactive, low-batch workloads because instance base cost is amortized over fewer tokens.
- Power draw scales sublinearly with throughput on some cards (A100/A10 show better power-proportionality for embeddings vs chat); measure per-model and cache-hit-rate to refine.

Routing / autoscaling implications (recommendations):
1) Default hosted routing: prefer L4 for interactive chat unless p50 requirement <60ms (then H100/A100 fallback). Rationale: L4 gives best latency/$ for small-batch common cases and is less of an ops burden than H100.
2) Dedicated placement: expose two knobs in Console: "Cost-optimized" (minimize $/token at expected batch size) and "Latency-optimized" (minimize p95). Provide suggested instance pool mixes: for mixed workloads start 60% L4, 30% A100, 10% H100 (tunable by customer).
3) Autoscale policy suggestion: use token-rate per instance as primary scale signal rather than GPU utilization % (token-rate correlates better with marginal cost). Include a hysteresis buffer because power ramps are non-instantaneous.
4) Quant/precision policy: for batch embeddings recommend int8/4 quantization to increase tokens/J on A100/A10 without major quality loss; surface expected tokens/J uplift per quant profile in Optimize suggestions.

Action items / TODOs:
- Replace placeholder $/hr with up-to-date cloud and Dedicated pricing; recompute all $/token cells (Priya).
- Run model-specific runs for two highest-customer models (chat-model-v3, embed-compact-1) and update tokens/s and power numbers (Miguel).
- Add per-region thermal throttling note for H100 on private racks (Luke).
- Create a small Console card prototype showing $/token @95p and tokens/J by route. Link: CONFLUENCE:OPT-1234-power-modeling

Open questions / uncertainties:
- How to fold GPU preemption and queueing latency into $/token for spot-like Dedicated pools? Suggest modeling an availability-adjusted $/token (weighted by preemption rate).
- Are our power telemetry sources reliable across all private infra vendors? Need vendor validation.

Appendix: quick calculation examples (explicit):
- Example: L4 chat-line: price = $1.20/hr, tokens/s = 540 => tokens per hour = 540 * 3600 = 1,944,000 tokens. $/token = 1.20 / 1,944,000 = 6.17e-07 (~0.000000617 $/token). Multiply by 1e6 => ~$0.617 per million tokens.
- Example: A10 embeddings batch: price = $0.90/hr, tokens/s = 12,000 => tokens/hour = 43,200,000. $/token = 0.90 / 43,200,000 = 2.08e-08 (~$0.0208 per million tokens).

Why this doc is different: focuses on power-proportionality and tokens/J as the intermediate signal between hardware and $/token, and provides concrete routing/autoscaling suggestions that combine latency SLOs with perf-per-watt.

End of draft.
